findings.summary: The rotation's own documented flow writes to the checkout that integrity drift forbids, so it trips operator-only recovery
findings.recommendation: Resume re-fingerprints the checkout: HEAD, the status digest, the tracked diff and every untracked file (`_integrityDrift` -> `checkoutFingerprint.compare`). Any difference is integrity drift that no receipt can accept, and it leaves abandon as the only next command. Three steps of the rotation's own flow change exactly those inputs. (1) Clear mode: the re-entry turn (`renderReentry` step 4) and `docs/coordinator-rotation.md` tell the replacement to 'write the receipt JSON ... and run `tc rotation resume --receipt <file>`' without saying where. A receipt written in the checkout, the natural place, is a new untracked file, so `checkout.untracked:<file>` plus `statusDigest` drift and resume is always refused. (2) Prepare: a checkpoint file saved in the checkout is undeclared dirt. The coordinator must list it in its own `ownedDirt`, and deleting it afterwards is drift. (3) Relaunch mode: the documented way the old session ends is 'a wrap'. The wrap pipeline's `commit` step cannot be disabled (`lib/wrap-step-overrides.js` UNDISABLEABLE_KINDS) and commits whenever memory, priming or the version changed. That moves HEAD, so `checkout.head` drifts and every wrap-ended relaunch rotation needs the operator. The relaunch tests end the old session with `store.sessions.wrap` and stub the fingerprint, so neither path is exercised. Scope: class, meaning every step of the rotation that writes to the fingerprinted checkout. Fix it at one point: tell the replacement to write the receipt outside the checkout (or have `tc rotation resume` read stdin), and decide explicitly how a relaunch's own wrap commit is baselined (re-fingerprint at claim, or accept a fast-forward of the checkpoint head made by the wrap). findings.summary: Epoch binding outlives the bound session's normal end, and 'released' is modelled as 'abandoned'
findings.recommendation: What happens: after a clear-mode rotation reaches `active`, gate() binds every gated action to that rotation's session, launch and thread, and nothing ends the binding except a new rotation or an operator abandon (lib/coordinator-rotation.js gate(), store latestForProject). A coordinator that later wraps normally, which the bound replacement is allowed to do, and is relaunched the next day finds `tc workload set`, Medusa send/ack/close, control, session-rule writes and wrap all refused with COORDINATOR_EPOCH_MISMATCH. Its way out is either an operator abandon of a rotation that actually succeeded, or a `tc rotation prepare` that /clears a fresh session with nothing to checkpoint. The refusal text offers both. So the routine wrap-and-relaunch cycle of any coordinator that has rotated once needs the operator every time. The release path also records the successful rotation as `abandoned` with failureCode 'abandoned', which erases the success from history and drops currentGeneration(). Why it broke: the binding's lifetime is keyed to the latest rotation row, not to the lifecycle of the session it binds. Scope: instance. Remedy: (a) have the gate lapse the binding once the bound session has ended through its own completed wrap (the gate already computes `ended` for its message), or (b) add a distinct terminal state such as `released` so an epoch release is not recorded as a failed rotation. Either way, get the Architect to confirm against rulings A2/A11/A12, since docs/coordinator-rotation.md currently records the lifetime as 'until a governed next rotation ... or the operator abandons'.

findings.summary: A new thread seen before any /clear now stalls the rotation forever as a retryable wait
findings.recommendation: instance. In _rebindStep (lib/coordinator-rotation.js:826), `settling` is true when `rotation.lastClearAttemptAt` is unset. When the prior thread is still loaded and a new root thread appears before the driver has typed any /clear (for example, the operator opens a thread in the project directory), the `prior && fresh.length === 0` branch is skipped, so no clear is attempted. Every later pass therefore returns `prior-thread-unloading` with no time bound. That code is not in OPERATOR_FAILURES, so nextCommand stays `tc rotation advance` indefinitely. Before this delta the same picture ended in `prior-thread-still-loaded`, which is operator-only. The docs say the window runs 'after an admitted clear', and no test covers the no-clear case. Fix: treat a missing lastClearAttemptAt as outside the window (`settling = !!rotation.lastClearAttemptAt && now - last < REBIND_WINDOW_MS`). Then add a test in which a new root thread appears before any clear and the rotation reaches `prior-thread-still-loaded` without looping. Related: _attemptClear also stamps lastClearAttemptAt on a refused (not admitted) attempt, so the window currently starts from any attempt rather than an admitted one. Decide whether that is intended when you make the fix.
